title_topic: Corticosteroids in septic shock and severe pneumonia
summary: In septic shock, ADRENAL (3,800 ventilated patients, hydrocortisone infusion) showed faster shock resolution but no 90-day mortality benefit, while APROCCHSS (1,241 sicker patients, hydrocortisone boluses plus enteral fludrocortisone) cut 90-day mortality from 49% to 43%. The 2023 individual-patient meta-analysis found no overall mortality effect, with a signal only for regimens that included fludrocortisone. Observational target-trial emulation supports adding fludrocortisone, but a 2024 phase II dose-finding trial did not, and RECORDS is still recruiting. In severe community-acquired pneumonia, CAPE COD (hydrocortisone, which excluded shock and influenza) halved 28-day mortality. REMAP-CAP's open-label 7-day hydrocortisone arm stopped for futility with a numerically worse result, and its population, allocation and control-arm contamination all differ from CAPE COD. ESCAPe (methylprednisolone) was neutral. On who benefits: in a 2025 individual-patient meta-analysis the benefit was confined to patients with CRP above 204 mg/L. Post hoc transcriptomic (SRS2, consensus subtype CTS2) and biomarker (CAPE COD reanalysis) work suggests immune-profile-dependent benefit or harm, but none of it is ready for the bedside. On guidelines: SSC 2026 gives a conditional suggestion for steroids in septic shock. SCCM 2024 is conditional for shock and strong for severe CAP. ERS/ESICM 2023 supports steroids in severe CAP only with shock and predates CAPE COD. ATS 2025 (without IDSA) reverses the 2019 ATS/IDSA advice with a conditional yes for severe CAP. NICE NG250 (2025) says consider them for high-severity CAP, IV hydrocortisone first, for 4 to 7 days.
takeaways: In septic shock, hydrocortisone reliably shortens shock; any survival benefit is small and may depend on adding fludrocortisone.
In severe CAP without shock or influenza, CAPE COD supports early hydrocortisone, and NICE (2025) and the ATS (2025) now agree.
REMAP-CAP means you shouldn't assume the CAPE COD benefit carries over to patients with shock or to later starts.
High CRP is the best bedside hint of who benefits; biomarker and gene-expression subtypes aren't ready for clinical use.
Watch glucose and sodium, and document why you started.
